title: Jus de Madd, Casamance Madd Fruit Juice
author: Chef Bineta Diallo Dioh (Slow Food Foundation for Biodiversity with FAO)
desc: 500 g of madd inner fruit, 1 litre of water and sugar to taste, chilled — the entire printed recipe for the juice of the orange-fleshed Casamance vine fruit.
longDesc: The Slow Food and FAO booklet ‘Sénégal: de la terre à la table’ gives jus de madd as three ingredients — 500 g of madd (Saba senegalensis) inner fruit, 1 litre of water, sugar to taste — and says to chill the juice afterwards. NOTHING ELSE IS PRINTED: no temperatures, no times, no yield and no doneness cue, and the research notes record no method for extracting the inner fruit. FAO’s separate feature story on the fruit (11 August 2025, no byline) records that the fruit is gathered ‘by hand or with poles’ from vines sometimes over 40 metres tall, that local communities mainly eat it fresh, that only about two percent of collected fruit is processed into juices and preserves, and that the Madd de Casamance geographical indication was registered on 25 June 2024.
ingredients: Sugar, to taste — quantity not printed
steps: Extract the inner fruit of the madd. The source records no method for this step.
Combine the 500 g of inner fruit with the 1 litre of water and sweeten to taste. The source records no method for combining, straining or timing.
chefTips: The recipe prints no times, temperatures or cues.
Taste the sweetness yourself — ‘sugar to taste’ is the only guide.
Chill thoroughly; the booklet only says to chill.
commonMistakes: Expecting a method the source does not print.
servedWith: Cereal porridge (juice is often drunk with it, per the FAO feature)
healthBenefits: Madd is eaten fresh and processed into juices and sweet and savoury preserves.
culturalNote: ‘Madd fruits are deeply rooted in the culture of the lower Casamance region.’ (FAO). The FAO story names no ethnic group.
sources: Primary: Slow Food Foundation for Biodiversity with FAO, ‘Sénégal: de la terre à la table’ (recipes credited to chef Bineta Diallo Dioh; directed by Velia Lucidi and Serena Milano; texts Serena Berisio). No date printed. Jus de Madd: 500 g inner fruit, 1 litre of water, sugar to taste; ‘chill’ with no figure. TWO-PASS AGREED; yield none printed (4 used for scheduling).
Context: FAO Feature Story, ‘Mad for ‘Madd de Casamance’’, 11/08/2025, no byline, SINGLE-PASS — about two percent of collected fruit processed; GI registered 25 June 2024; fruit up to 10 cm.
ABSENT: extraction method, straining, times, temperatures, sugar quantity. The 20-minute prep is a scheduling estimate.
